prerequisites: The student has a solid knowledge of computer and network infrastructure and knowledge of virtualization.

learning_outcomes.text: At the end of this course, the student has in-depth theoretical and practical knowledge about high availability. The student has in-depth knowledge about the different techniques and concepts of high availability.

At the end of this course, the student can install, manage, and deliver existing high availability solutions. The student can install and configure an existing high availability solution. The student can adapt the configuration to the needs of the users. The student can optimize the system according to the available hardware. The student can test the proper functioning of the system. The student reports clearly and distinctly on the settings and management of the system.
The student can work purposefully and efficiently in a team. The student communicates and consults with other team members regarding the technical and organizational aspects of the work.

syllabus_topics: Concepts and definitions of high availability
High Availability in a virtualization environment
Development of redundant and highly available systems and environments using virtual machines

assessment_methods.method: Theory exam (written exam, open questions, closed book)
Lab (presentation / demonstration of the results of the lab assignments)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a theory exam (40%) and lab assignments (60%). Partial transfers are possible for successful components (Theory and Lab) within the academic year. For resits, the same weighting applies: 40% for theory (written exam) and 60% for lab (one or more assignments depending on previous scores). No demonstration during lab sessions results in no points for the assignment.
